facts.statement: Saurophaganax is a dubious and chimeric genus of large saurischian dinosaur that may have been a sauropod.
facts.quote: Saurophaganax ("lord of lizard-eaters") is a dubious, chimeric genus of large saurischian dinosaur, possibly a sauropod, from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of Oklahoma, United States.

facts.statement: The name Saurophagus maximus was coined in 1941 by John Willis Stovall.
facts.quote: In 1941, these were named Saurophagus maximus by Stovall in an article by journalist Grace Ernestine Ray.

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Danison and colleagues re-evaluated the specimens assigned to Saurophaganax maximus.
facts.quote: In 2024, Danison and colleagues revised the referral of various specimens assigned to Saurophaganax maximus including the fragmentary holotype neural arch (OMNH 1123) based on their comparative analysis.

facts.statement: The taxonomic placement of Saurophaganax is unstable, with studies suggesting it could be related to Metriacanthosauridae, Allosauria, or Carcharodontosauria.
facts.quote: In 2019, Rauhut and colleagues noted that the definitive taxonomic placement of Saurophaganax within Allosauroidea is unstable, being recovered as a sister taxon of Metriacanthosauridae or Allosauria, or even as a basalmost carcharodontosaurian.

facts.statement: A 2024 reassessment suggested that the allosaurid specimens previously assigned to Saurophaganax belong to a new species of Allosaurus named Allosaurus anax.
facts.quote: Re-evaluation of the assigned specimens in a 2024 reassessment suggested that the referred allosaurid specimens belong to a novel species of Allosaurus, named as Allosaurus anax.

facts.statement: Saurophaganax lived in the Late Jurassic, specifically within the Kimmeridgian stage of the Morrison Formation, which dates from approximately 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Morrison Formation is a sequence of shallow marine and alluvial sediments which, according to radiometric dating, ranges between 156.3 million years old (Ma) at its base, to 146.8 million years old at the top, which places it in the late Oxfordian, Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The Morrison Basin, where Saurophaganax fossils were found, stretched from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: The Morrison Basin where dinosaurs lived, stretched from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan, and was formed when the precursors to the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains started pushing up to the west.

facts.statement: The environment where Saurophaganax lived was a semiarid region with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: This formation is interpreted as a semiarid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Very little is known about the behavior of Saurophaganax due to the rarity of its fossil remains.
facts.quote: Because of the rarity of discovered remains, not much about its behavior is known.

facts.statement: Saurophaganax is currently classified as incertae sedis, meaning its family placement is uncertain.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: incertae sedis

facts.statement: Saurophaganax was a large saurischian dinosaur, possibly a sauropod, from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Oklahoma.
facts.quote: Fue un dinosaurio saurisquio de gran tamaño, posiblemente un saurópodo, del Jurásico superior de la Formación Morrison de Oklahoma, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: John Willis Stovall discovered remains of a large dinosaur near Kenton in Cimarron County, Oklahoma, in the latest Kimmeridgian layers between 1931 and 1932.
facts.quote: En 1931 y 1932, John Willis Stovall descubrió restos de un gran dinosaurio cerca de Kenton en el condado de Cimarron, Oklahoma, en capas del último Kimmeridgiano.

facts.statement: In 1941, John Willis Stovall named the remains "Saurophagus maximus" in an article by journalist Grace Ernestine Ray.
facts.quote: En 1941, Stovall los denominó "Saurophagus maximus" en un artículo de la periodista Grace Ernestine Ray.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from Greek words meaning "lizard" and "to eat", combining to mean "lizard-eater".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego σαυρος, sauros , "lagarto" y φάγειν , phagein, "comer", con el significado compuesto de "comedor de lagartos".

facts.statement: The specific epithet maximus means "the largest" in Latin.
facts.quote: El epíteto maximus específico significa "el más grande" en latín.

facts.statement: In 1987, Spencer George Lucas incorrectly designated OMNH 4666, a tibia, as the lectotype of Saurophagus without realizing the genus was invalid.
facts.quote: En 1987, Spencer George Lucas hizo erróneamente de OMNH 4666, una tibia, el lectotipo, sin saber que Saurophagus era un inválido.

facts.statement: In 1995, Daniel Chure established the new genus Saurophaganax by adding the Greek suffix meaning "ruler" to the previous name.
facts.quote: En 1995, Daniel Chure nombró un nuevo género, Saurophaganax , agregando el sufijo griego -άναξ, anax , que significa "gobernante", al nombre anterior.

facts.statement: Daniel Chure selected OMNH 01123, a neural arch, as the holotype for Saurophaganax because he found the previous specimen OMNH 4666 was not diagnostic compared to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Chure también encontró que OMNH 4666 no era diagnóstico en relación con Allosaurus, por lo que eligió OMNH 01123, un arco neural, como el holotipo de Saurophaganax.

facts.statement: While the most known Saurophaganax material was found in Oklahoma, a possible partial skeleton including a femur, tail vertebrae, and a hip bone was found in northern New Mexico.
facts.quote: Aunque el material de Saurophaganax más conocido se encontró en el territorio de Oklahoma, en el norte de Nuevo México se ha encontrado un posible material de Saurophaganax, NMMNH P-26083, un esqueleto parcial que incluye un fémur, varias vértebras de la cola y un hueso de la cadera.

facts.statement: In 2024, Danison and colleagues reviewed the assignment of specimens to Saurophaganax maximus, including the fragmentary holotype neural arch OMNH 1123, based on their comparative analysis.
facts.quote: En 2024, Danison y sus colegas revisaron la referencia de varios especímenes asignados a Saurophaganax maximus, incluido el arco neural del holotipo fragmentario, OMNH 1123, basándose en su análisis comparativo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that the holotype could not be confidently identified as a theropod or sauropod, although complex accessory laminae are more comparable to sauropods, especially juvenile Apatosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Sugirieron que el holotipo no podía considerarse con seguridad como un terópodo o un saurópodo, aunque las complejas láminas accesorias son más comparables a las de los saurópodos, especialmente algunos especímenes juveniles de Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Some referred specimens likely belong to diplodocids rather than the large allosaurid from the Kenton 1 quarry.
facts.quote: Algunos especímenes referidos probablemente pertenecen más bien a diplodócidos que al gran alosáurido de la cantera Kenton 1.

facts.statement: Because the holotype neural arch is so fragmentary, researchers could not refer it confidently to a theropod or sauropod, leading them to consider Saurophaganax maximus dubious.
facts.quote: Dado que el arco neural del holotipo es tan fragmentario, los investigadores no podían referirlo con seguridad a un terópodo o un saurópodo, por lo que consideran que Saurophaganax maximus es dudoso.

facts.statement: Saurophaganax belongs to the parent group Allosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Allosauridae

facts.statement: Saurophaganax is classified in the family Allosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Allosauridae

facts.statement: Saurophaganax is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Saurophaganax is Saurophaganax maximus.
facts.quote: Type species: Saurophaganax maximus

facts.statement: Saurophaganax lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Remains of Saurophaganax were found in the latest Kimmeridgian layers near Kenton in Cimarron County, Oklahoma.
facts.quote: En 1931 y 1932, John Willis Stovall descubrió restos de un gran dinosaurio cerca de Kenton en el condado de Cimarron, Oklahoma, en capas del último Kimmeridgiano.

rejected.quote: In 1995, Daniel Chure named a new genus Saurophaganax, adding Greek suffix -άναξ, which means "ruler", replacing the earlier informal name "Saurophagus".
